items: Alluvial soil is rich in potash but generally deficient in nitrogen, phosphorus, and organic humus content.
Black soil exhibits a unique 'self-ploughing' property because it develops deep cracks during the dry season, promoting aeration.
Bangar represents older alluvium containing calcareous deposits called 'Kankar', whereas Khadar is newer, more fertile riverbed alluvium.
Red soil gets its distinctive color from the diffusion of iron in crystalline and metamorphic rocks, turning yellow when hydrated.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Pedology is the branch of soil science that focuses on soil formation, morphology, and classification in its natural environment.
The Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR) classifies Indian soils into 8 major groups, with Alluvial soil being the most fertile and widespread.
Black soil (Regur) is rich in clay content and retains moisture well, making it exceptionally suited for cotton cultivation in the Deccan Plateau.
Laterite soil forms under conditions of high temperature and heavy rainfall through intense leaching (desilication), leaving behind iron and aluminum oxides.
Soil profile layers are ordered sequentially from top to bottom as Horizon O (Organic), Horizon A (Topsoil), Horizon B (Subsoil), Horizon C (Weathered Parent Rock), and Horizon R (Bedrock).
